verses.text: From Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by God's will, and from our brother Timothy. I write to God's church in Corinth, and to all God's holy people everywhere in Achaia.
Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Praise be to the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. He is the Father who shows mercy, and the God who gives all comfort.
He comforts us in all our troubles. Then we can comfort others in any trouble, with the same comfort God has given us.
We share a lot in the sufferings of Christ. In the same way, we also share a lot of comfort through Christ.
If we have trouble, it is for your comfort and for your saving. If we are comforted, it is for your comfort too. It helps you to bear patiently the same sufferings that we bear.
Our hope for you is firm. We know that as you share in our sufferings, you also share in our comfort.
Brothers and sisters, we want you to know about the trouble we had in the province of Asia. The load on us was far too heavy for our strength, so that we even gave up hope of staying alive.
In our hearts we felt we had been sentenced to death. But this happened so that we would not trust in ourselves, but in God, who raises the dead.
He saved us from such a terrible danger of death, and he will save us again. We have put our hope in him, that he will keep on saving us.
You help us too by praying for us. Then many people will thank God for the kindness he shows us because so many prayed.

This is what we are proud of. Our conscience tells us that we have lived in the world, and even more with you, in a holy and honest way that comes from God. We did not live by worldly wisdom, but by God's grace.
We write to you only what you can read and understand. And I hope you will understand fully,
as you have already understood us in part. Then on the day of our Lord Jesus you will be proud of us, just as we will be proud of you.
Because I was sure of this, I planned to visit you first, so that you would be blessed twice.
I planned to visit you on my way to Macedonia, and again on my way back from Macedonia. Then you could send me on my way to Judea.
When I made this plan, did I change my mind too easily? Do I make my plans the way worldly people do, ready to say "Yes, yes" and "No, no" at the same time?
As surely as God is faithful, what we told you was not "Yes" and "No" at the same time.
Jesus Christ, the Son of God, whom Silas, Timothy and I preached to you, was not "Yes" and "No." In him it has always been "Yes."
However many promises God has made, they are all "Yes" in Christ. That is why we say "Amen" through him, to bring glory to God.
It is God who makes both us and you stand firm in Christ. He has anointed us.
He has put his mark of ownership on us, and he has put his Spirit in our hearts as a first payment of what is to come.
I call on God as my witness that I did not come back to Corinth because I wanted to spare you.
We are not trying to rule over your faith. We are working with you for your joy, because you stand firm in your faith.
